newsitem.title: GERMANY: Cocoa consumers seen buying in H1 1997 -importer.
newsitem.headline: Cocoa consumers seen buying in H1 1997 -importer.

text.p: Major chocolate manufacturers are likely to extend their cocoa cover in the first half of 1997 after winding down their cover in comfortable supply conditions last year, German importer KEG said on Monday.
A market report distributed to KEG customers said the industry would try and anticipate upcoming deficit years.
British manufacturers were seen taking advantage of the strong pound, which offered them better buying power.
KEG also said the Ivorian marketing agency, the Caisse de Stabilisation, was expected to reduce its auctions, which could underpin near term prices.
But elsewhere, lacking fund buying interest and the anticipated liquidation of a massive long position held by one key operator were seen limiting the cocoa price upside.
KEG also pointed out that cocoa stocks were ample.

European stocks at the end of November -- before the arrival from the West African new crops -- had been at 648,000 tonnes, up from 637,600 in October and up by 61,000 tonnes from the previous record level in 1993, it said.
It cited figures from SGS Warehouse Services.
KEG pegged 1996/97 world cocoa output at 2.61 million tonnes, down by seven percent from 95/96, based on its own calculations.
It forecast a supply deficit of 120,000 tonnes in the 96/97 season after an estimated 130,000 tonnes surplus in 95/96.
